item.text: {"summary":"The draft is substantively well-formed, but publication should block until the resolver fields align with the registered ledger target contract or the ledger discrepancy is handled explicitly without changing the target fields.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"blocking","summary":"The draft uses resolutionDate 2026-09-29 and resolutionSourceUrl jolts.t01.htm, while the registered target contract supplied for review binds the target to the ledger registration/sourceBinding with window end 2026-10-05 and sourceUrl https://www.bls.gov/news.release/jolts.nr0.htm.","actionRequested":"Set the published JSON resolver fields to the registered target contract values, or if treating the BLS calendar date as a ledger error, keep the target tied to the registered slug/dataPointId and state the discrepancy in reasoning without silently substituting incompatible resolver fields."},{"rubricItem":"coherence","severity":"warning","summary":"The reasoning says the ledger window ends 2026-10-05 but the JSON uses 2026-09-29, creating ambiguity about whether this is a release-calendar target or a resolve-by-bound registered target.","actionRequested":"Make the final forecast step and JSON fields use one target contract consistently, with any ledger/date discrepancy called out as a note rather than changing the target identity."}],"optionalSuggestions":["The prior/update/interval step is compact and names the persistence prior, sample, adjustments, sigma method, and bounds.","Tail scenarios are concrete enough; adding one sentence on why two-month widening from 0.51 to 0.65 is calibrated would strengthen the interval rationale."]}
